newsitem.title: UK: BA prepared to give EU more detail on US link.
newsitem.headline: BA prepared to give EU more detail on US link.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Tuesday it was ready to supply more information to the European Commission for its investigation into BA's proposed alliance with American Airlines if the Commission requested it.
European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said in Brussels on Tuesday he was waiting for BA and American to provide supplementary information on their planned link-up.
"If the European Commission requires any further information, of course we would be only to happy to supply the information," said BA spokesman David Wilson.
He said BA had already given the Commission a significant amount of detail but if they needed further clarification BA would supply it.
"We have provided all of the information that the EU has required to date but if it requires more we'll put it in to them." He said BA had no indication when the EU might make a decision.

Britain has objected to the EU's role in investigating the deal, originally proposed last June. Britain's competition watchdog the Office of Fair Trading has provisionally approved the alliance on condition that BA give up 168 weekly takeoff and landing slots at London's Heathrow airport.

There has been press speculation that BA would be prepared to give up some of its slots, but only if it could sell them for a fair price. Van Miert has stated his opposition to BA profiting from the handover of its Heathrow facilities.
